channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Torres strikes again as PSG beat bitter rivals Marseille 2-1
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain claimed the bragging rights in 'Le Classique' on Sunday, edging Marseille 2-1 as Spaniard Ferran Torres scored his seventh goal in six appearances for his new club.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Russia's ruling party on track to win election after Ukraine's drone attacks on Moscow
item.description: Russia's ruling United Russia party on Sunday was projected to win the country's tightly controlled parliamentary elections, according to exit polls. Ukraine launched a massive drone attack on Moscow, killing three people, said city officials, on the third and final day of Russia's wartime vote.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Macron, Carney hail new chapter in France-Canada ties at symbolic archipelago meeting
item.description: French President ​Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on ​Sunday called for stronger bilateral ties in the face of new global threats at a meeting on Saint Pierre and Miquelon, a French territory off Canada's Newfoundland. The first-ever visit by a Canadian leader to the North Atlantic archipelago came as both countries have increasingly awkward relations with the US.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Replay: Macron, Carney hail new chapter on France-Canada ties at St. Pierre and Miquelon meeting
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said France and Canada were "two great independent nations who want to stay that way" in a joint news conference with Canadian leader Mark Carney Sunday. Watch the press conference by the two leaders on the French overseas territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon just off Canada's Atlantic coast.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Germany: Merz vows to "push on despite setbacks"
item.description: German voters have delivered a fresh setback to Chancellor Friedrich Merz in two key regional elections.
item.dc:creator: Clémence WALLER

item.title: The Deportation Project: Inside the Trump administration's secret deals to expel people worldwide
item.description: A consortium of 72 journalists from 26 media outlets coordinated by Forbidden Stories have been working on the Deportation Project for months. On Monday, we will take you inside the Trump administration's secret deals to expel people worldwide.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Exit polls show 'disaster' for Merz' CDU party in two state elections
item.description: Germans headed to the polls today in two state elections - in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Exit polls suggest a dramatic loss for the Chancellor Freidrich Mertz's Christian Democratic Union party. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Berlin, Jörg Taszman.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Germany’s Merz admits ‘disaster’ in state elections, vows to press ahead with reforms
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Sunday described his CDU party's heavy losses in two regional elections as a "disaster", but vowed to push ahead with a reform drive. The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party took first place in ​the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, exit polls showed, and also gained in strength in another election in Berlin.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Israeli settler and Palestinian driver killed in West Bank shootings
item.description: A suspected Palestinian gunman on Sunday shot dead an Israeli man near a West Bank settlement, according to Israeli officials. The gunman was located at a Ramallah hospital and arrested, police said. Elsewhere in the West Bank, Israeli soldiers killed a Palestinian motorist who the military said was attempting to run them over. The flare up in violence came on the eve of the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: AfD threatens fresh blow to Merz: Two German states hold key vote
item.description: Two German states are heading to the polls today – in Berlin and the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. The far-right AfD party is expected to make further gains after securing a historic win in Saxony-Anhalt two weeks ago, though it has no realistic path to power in Berlin. Sunday's vote is a key test for Chancellor Friedrich Merz, one that could determine whether he can hold on to power. Details with Jamie Smith-Maillet, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ukraine fires over 1,000 drones at Russia in "largest ever" attack on Moscow
item.description: Russia is completing its three-day vote for the Duma this Sunday – the first since its large-scale invasion of Ukraine. The election was organised for the first time also in the Ukrainian regions occupied by Russia, and it was marked by Ukrainian drone strikes at various areas - mainly Moscow. Details by Shirli Sitbon.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: An Israeli settler and a Palestinian driver killed in West Bank shootings
item.description: An Israeli settler has been fatally shot in the occupied West Bank, while Israel's military said it killed a man who attempted to ram his vehicle into troops elsewhere in the Palestinian territory. The news came as violence in the West Bank is escalating at a very rapid pace. “All Israeli military authorities involved with the West Bank have been warning the Israeli government that the situation is basically out of control”, explains FRANCE 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Iran closes French language centre in Tehran for ‘illegal acts’
item.description: Iranian authorities on Sunday shut down the French Language Centre (CLF) in Tehran, alleging the French embassy-linked institute conducted "illegal acts that violated diplomatic conventions" and "abused its status as a language training facility". France has vowed to take "appropriate measures" in response.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: The week in pictures: Syria protests, Céline Dion on stage and Quito wildfires
item.description: From protests against rising fuel prices in Syria to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s EU charm offensive to Quito’s wildfires and Céline Dion’s return to the stage, FRANCE 24 looks back at the week's most striking pictures.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Houthi attacks and no Western support: What are Saudi Arabia's options ?
item.description: The US has warned that fighting between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthis could rapidly escalate. It comes after a missile attack targeted Riyadh for the first time since the Yemen conflict resumed. The Houthis' lightning offensive seized swathes of Yemeni territory in recent weeks and has left hundreds dead. In the face of such attacks and with no support from its American ally, what are Saudi Arabia’s options?
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'NAZA' documentary about Gaza war sparks political storm in Israel
item.description: The Israeli filmmakers behind the documentary NAZA may have received a standing ovation at the Venice film festival, they have been facing violent threats to their lives and citizenship at home in Israel. A month ahead of crucial elections, the film profiles anonymous military sources who speak about the widespread killing of civilians in Gaza. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he intends to introduce legislation aimed at revoking the citizenship of people who "defame IDF soldiers". Details by Shirli Sitbon, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Why doesn't the US intervene to defend Saudi Arabia against the Houthis?
item.description: The US cautioned against a rapidly escalating situation in Yemen after Houthi rebels carried out a missile attack on the Saudi capital. In recent weeks, the Iran backed militants have also seized large portions of Yemeni territory following clashes with Saudi-backed government forces. The US is a very close ally to Saudi Arabia. Yet, is visibly unwilling to intervene on its behalf – why? Details and analysis by H. A. Hellyer, senior fellow in geopolitics at the Royal United Institute in Cairo.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: North Korea fires two ballistic missiles into the sea in latest weapons display
item.description: North Korea fired two short-range ballistic missiles into the sea off its eastern coast on Sunday, South Korea’s military said. This came days after Pyongyang reaffirmed its status as a nuclear-armed state and rejected a UN resolution calling for an end to its nuclear activities.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Germany: Could regional polls force Friedrich Merz to step down?
item.description: Polling is underway in the German capital Berlin and the largely rural state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania for regional elections. Both elections are seen as a test for Germany's centre-right Chancellor Friedrich Merz. He has already scheduled a crisis meeting and decided to skip this week's UN General Assembly to deal with the potential fallout. Could he be forced to step down based on the election’s results? Details and analysis by Yann Wernert, senior policy fellow at the Jacques Delors Centre in Berlin.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ukraine hits Russia with major drone attack, targeting refinery
item.description: In Russia, voters are on the third and final day of casting ballots in the country's first wartime parliamentary election. Despite the voting however, Ukraine carried out what Moscow described as the "largest ever" drone attack on the Russian capital. Kyiv reportedly fired over 1.000 drones at the country, leaving two dead in the Moscow region and inflicting damage upon an oil refinery. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Kyiv, Gulliver Cragg.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Nine women found dead near Johannesburg sends shockwaves through South Africa
item.description: Vigils, group runs and moments of silence: thousands of protesters gathered across South Africa this weekend to pay tribute to the nine women found murdered in eastern Johannesburg. In a country that records more than 60 homicides a day, the nine murders sent shockwaves through the population. Anger is mounting, and calls are growing for the government to take action. Story by Caroline Baum.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ed Sheeran calls Gaza war catastrophic after dropping Macklemore over pro-Palestinian comments
item.description: English singer Ed Sheeran opened his first show since his opener Macklemore was dropped after making pro-Palestinian comments onstage. The move sparked controversy and prompted several other support acts to drop out of the tour, publishing statements citing their support for Palestinians. While some concert goers could be seen trying to sell their tickets on Saturday, others have voiced their support for the 'Shape of You' singer. Story by Charlotte Hughes.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Three media outlets barred from the White House over 'fake news'
item.description: Donald Trump has suggested that more news outlets may be barred from the White House after he announced he was banning Politico, CNN and MS NOW. On Saturday, all three outlets said that the White House confiscated their teams' press passes; they have also hinted at legal action. The ban has come under sharp criticism from press freedom advocates, as Charlotte Hughes explains.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US and Denmark reach Greenland security deal
item.description: The US and Denmark have announced a deal on Greenland's security, resolving a diplomatic dispute sparked by President Donald Trump when he threatened to seize the semi-autonomous territory. The exact terms of the deal remain uncertain but it seems Denmark will maintain its sovereignty while the US will be able to develop a significant military presence on the island, and ban their adversaries from building their own bases on the island. Details by Charlotte Hughes.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
